why: Commit 1 (copyToLibrary carries ai_marked_at through libraryFilesByUrl, the only builder) and commit 3 (retire one dispatcher job after an owner-run count) are small and exact. Commit 2 replaces commerce.cron_due(), a function step 3.1 has not written yet, 'in exactly the form the function uses for page-jobs'. It also adds two indexes on invoice tables in a migration CI applies to production. A wrong copy of the function would pass a local int test but could stop or flood every queue of the one-minute tick.
harm_if_wrong: A mistaken cron_due() replacement could drop another queue from the tick, or call the 102 MB Chromium PDF route every minute for ever, and it would be applied to production by CI without a hand check.
make_it_cheaper: Once step 3.1 has landed, quote cron_due()'s current body in the brief and give the new branch as a literal diff against it.
brief_problems: Commit 2 depends on the shape of commerce.cron_due() and on step 3.1's int-test helper, neither of which exists yet. stop_if covers the first, but the executor has to infer 'the same form as page-jobs'.
